note:
R96 - decoding-contract validation matrix for gen7 `.ast` streams (queue 1 of the 2026-09-25 continuation). Cases are SELECTED
from the R91 per-stream summary so that every (platform, codec, rate, channel_config, loop form, block-count bucket) class of the
corpus has a decoded member where the class is decodable, plus named boundary cases (single-block X360 streams whose first block is
terminal, PS3 4-granule terminal trims, the 6-channel streams, the longest streams under the sample bound). Decoder acceptance only.

Per vector (reusing the R91 framing and the R92 decode routes):
  V1 declared vs decoded: EAL3 decoded == granules x 576 per sub-stream; XMA decoded == Σ block samples (+ the header +1000 control on
     multi-block XMA); V2 first block: decodable - declared == 1152 / 384 (non-terminal first block) and the WARM-UP region of the
     decoder output (0..1151 EAL3 / none XMA) characterised by rms; V3 middle-block continuity: restart decode from block k (k = middle)
     -> per-granule rms difference until it reaches 0 -> `transient_granules` (EAL3) / 0 (XMA); V4 channel ordering: for stereo
     sub-streams the block-0 PCM frame is compared with decoder output at 1105 under BOTH the interleaved and the planar reading
     (held-out records; the R92 result was 4 stereo vectors); V5 terminal: the trimmed-off flush (decoded beyond samples_sum + start)
     characterised (rms, zero fraction) - is it silence or audio?; V6 loops: stub decode == PCM-only output (a samples), body first
     delta, body tail; V7 a second MPEG decoder path (ffmpeg `mp3` integer vs `mp3float`) - same code base, different arithmetic:
     disclosed as NOT independent; max abs difference recorded.
Bounds: one ffmpeg process at a time, 180 s each, streams above MAX_SAMPLES skipped by name, no new WAV files.
Usage: python r96_decode_matrix.py <out.json> [--limit N]
ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 8.1.1-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers
